title: Run a fixed smoke set first
statement: Before any full run and after every change, run a small fixed smoke set end to end, and use it to find bugs, not to estimate rates.
example: A five-item probe surfaces format collapse and breakage for about 3% of a full run's cost.
detail: Two builds burned full 150-row grading runs before their collapse showed, one with 0 of 150 parsing and one 16.2 points down, so the project required a five-item smoke first: one item per type, drawn from the held-out pool and fixed across runs so results compare. A later backlog turns each recurring failure family into 3 to 5 fixed regression prompts run locally and live after every deploy, after five deploys had each carried an unverified gain claim. The set holds one item of each type plus a few per known failure family and runs through the whole make-and-check path.
against: A tiny smoke set cannot judge everything: a 7-response smoke showed question-set uniqueness of 1 of 2, which at that size was only a warning (icloud-work/aptraining-crystal-copy-20260521/evidence/RUN_MODE_TAXONOMY_AND_GATES_20260521.md, line 95).

evidence.quote: v38 (262 rows, eval=0/150 parse_ok) and v39 (1036 rows, −16.2pp binary) both burned the full 150-row IB-grader run before their collapse was visible.
A 5-item probe surfaces format collapse, deployment-side breakage, and obvious regressions for ~3% of the cost.

**Smoke composition.** 5 APUSH items, one per cell type (`MCQ`, `MCQ_SET`, `SAQ`, `DBQ`, `LEQ`), drawn from the held-out eval pool (NOT the training set). Items are fixed across runs so smoke results are comparable;
- Convert each family into 3-5 fixed regression prompts.
- Run them locally and live after every deploy.
**Value**: HIGH. Right now we have 5 deploys with no measured impact. Each deploy carries an unverified +N pp claim.
**Why this matters:** The 13K-row curriculum-API scaleup ($25-40) was gated on this 5-row pilot. The pilot worked — it found the bug cheaply. But the bug blocked the whole pipeline.
v44, v44b, v44d3 all produced 100% gen_fail.
A 10-item smoke test would have caught this.
The pilot's 100/80/20/10/0 spread was small-N noise on 5 cherry-picked cells.
